model_conventions.formal_meaning: The source's pointwise conditional-density notation for S given the continuously valued first report is represented by one rate-free regular conditional start kernel. Its support begins at the first report and it is conditionally independent of the supplied post-first-report tail; the fixed-history g(s) factor is separately rate independent.
model_conventions.why_needed: A literal probability P(S=t | T1=t1) is not a well-typed point-mass formula on a continuous carrier. Treating it as an unconditional scalar or as an arbitrary tail-dependent selector would lose the source's conditional and future-path independence content.
model_conventions.checked_scope: assumption_lemma2_condition_one_selection exposes the measurable first-report/start/tail maps, one Markov conditional start kernel, its support after the first report, its conditional law, and conditional tail independence. The Lemma 2 source theorem derives the stated exponential tail from that condition and a constructed forward Poisson process. The exact ten recursive field paths below are the only convention-credit routes; the source-model container and unrelated witness fields receive no inherited credit.

model_conventions.formal_meaning: Theorem 1's endpoint condition is read as one rate-free causal stopping policy: after a visible report prefix, its conditional endpoint-response law may use that prefix but cannot inspect a future report gap. The selected-start contribution is conditioned on the pre-start history and is rate free. A canonical finite trace samples one terminal endpoint, rather than a global family of independently resampled counterfactual endpoint clocks.
model_conventions.why_needed: The Appendix's terse final independence display can be misread as only a marginal statement after T1. The main theorem explicitly conditions on reports observed up to the endpoint and the application calls its end rule a stopping-times assumption. The live-history reading preserves those source semantics and is the minimum policy content needed for the likelihood calculation.
model_conventions.checked_scope: SourceTheoremModels.AppendixTheorem2CausalStoppingSourceModel exposes only a selected-start likelihood and visible-prefix endpoint kernels with measurability and nonnegative remaining-time support. CausalStoppingEndpointTrace constructs one endpoint from that policy, and PaperInterface.appendix_theorem2_eq8_causal_stopping_source_model derives the rate-free residual times the Poisson count PMF. The exact three endpoint-policy leaves below, and no density-presentation or container fields, receive this convention's source credit.

model_conventions.formal_meaning: The source's h_m(e) point-density notation is the absolutely-continuous presentation of an endpoint kernel. A deterministic cap or stopping endpoint can have an atom, so the general source model is a kernel law; the displayed scalar likelihood uses the explicitly supplied density presentation when the relevant endpoint branch is absolutely continuous.
model_conventions.why_needed: Treating every endpoint as Lebesgue-density-valued would silently exclude the fixed-cap observation policies described in the source application. Conversely, treating a point-density equation as a literal atom probability would not be a valid continuous likelihood statement.
model_conventions.checked_scope: The endpoint kernel is primary in AppendixTheorem2CausalStoppingSourceModel. EndpointDensityPresentation is an explicit AC presentation with a checked kernel-with-density equality. The canonical endpoint-law construction is atom safe, while the PaperInterface Eq. (8) theorem checks the scalar density factorization in exactly the source display's branch. Only the exact three density-presentation leaves below receive this convention's source credit; endpoint-policy and carrier fields do not.

model_conventions.formal_meaning: The marked-process route is a checked support theorem for the Appendix proof's birth-cohort interpretation: births in an interval receive iid eventual-report labels, and the retained-birth count is thinned. It is not a formalization of a calendar-window first-report process. The current source text does not define N_observed consistently enough to identify those two readings, and it does not derive the conditional duration/report-path survival identity used in p when lifetime may depend on report history.
model_conventions.why_needed: The distinction is semantic, not nominal: a first report in a window can come from a birth before that window. The existing marked interval law can support retained births but cannot establish a first-report displacement theorem. The source p calculation additionally needs duration/report-path independence or an equivalent conditional survival law; a duration density plus a marginal Poisson count law is insufficient.
model_conventions.checked_scope: The old scalar-rate model and the new cumulative-intensity birth-cohort model prove genuine marked-thinning support results. They do not receive full Lemma 1 or Proposition 1 source credit. The recursive field routes below are historical evidence for the scoped cohort model only and must be regenerated for the current source-record surface before any later closeout.

defects.status_impact_rationale: The reciprocal correction is an algebraic proof typo: the same rate-likelihood endpoint follows with the rate-free residual M!/(e-s)^M.
defects.repair_obligation: Match lambda^M exp(-lambda L) times the rate-free ordered-timeline density to exp(-lambda L)(lambda L)^M/M! and solve for the residual multiplier when L=e-s>0.
defects.acceptance_condition: Lean proves the residual multiplier is rate independent and equal to the corrected M!/(e-s)^M factor in the final Eq. (8) source wrapper.
defects.resolution_evidence: appendix_theorem2_eq8_causal_stopping_source_model exposes the corrected residual normalization and factors the source density into a rate-free term times the Poisson count PMF.

defects.source_locator: source.txt:1626-1812, Appendix B.1 Proposition 1 and Lemma 1
defects.source_claim: Lemma 1 asserts a steady-state observed Poisson process for independently reported incidents with a duration density; Proposition 1 uses that process and an iid unit-window law of large numbers to state nonidentifiability from observed unique-incident counts.
defects.status_impact_rationale: The checked models derive a retained-birth thinning process after receiving a marked interval law and a retention-probability equality. The source's data and simulation language instead uses calendar-time first reports, while its Appendix proof conditions on births in the same interval. The source also lacks the conditional duration/report-path survival condition needed for its displayed p calculation. Those are material model obligations, not ordinary zero-mass or notation conventions.
defects.repair_obligation: Choose and state the event-time semantics. For the birth-cohort reading, derive iid eventual-report marks from iid duration/report paths plus an explicit conditional survival identity and prove cross-window coherence. For calendar-time first reports, construct a two-sided stationary marked-displacement theorem from source-backed duration/report-path marks. In either route, do not accept the observed process, its interval law, or the p bridge as an unexamined source conclusion.
defects.acceptance_condition: A current paper-facing Lemma 1 route exposes the chosen source event semantics and derives its process law from source-backed primitives. A Proposition 1 route then derives its large-time limit and compensating-rate claim for that same semantics. The source map, record audit, and semantic judgment must all distinguish retained births from first-report arrivals.
